chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): A man has dirhams with me, and he meets me and asks, 'What is the price of the wadh (silver dirhams) today?' I say, 'Such and such.' He says, 'Do I not have such and such a thousand dirhams of wadh with you?' I say, 'Yes.' He says, 'Convert them for me into dinars at this price and keep them recorded with you.' What do you think of this?' He said to me, 'If you have determined the price for him on that day, there is no harm in that.' I said, 'I did not weigh them nor did I hand them over; it was merely speech between me and him.' He said, 'Are not the dirhams from you and the dinars from you?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then there is no harm.'

key_terms.أُنَاقِدْهُ: I hand it over / exchange it physically

ai.seo_question: Is currency exchange valid if the physical money is not immediately handed over?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) validates currency exchange (sarf) between dirhams and dinars based on verbal agreement without immediate physical exchange (qabd) or weighing, provided the price is fixed on that day. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the physical possession required for gold/silver and the contractual validity of recorded debts, emphasizing that mutual consent and fixed daily rates suffice for permissibility. It underscores the flexibility in commercial transactions within Islamic jurisprudence when dealing with monetary instruments.
